prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Katy, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1014; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give a recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You have my claim information.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in a parking lot at a shopping center in Katy, Texas. I was pulling into a space near the entrance.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I had just turned in and was going slowly, maybe five miles an hour. I was looking for an open spot.

Q: Describe the other vehicle.
A: It was a pickup truck. It was backing out of a spot two rows over, and it came across the lane toward me. I stopped as fast as I could, but it still hit the front corner of my car.

Q: Did you see the driver's face or hear anything before the contact?
A: No. I heard a horn briefly, maybe a second before. That's all I remember.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?
A: Not really. I felt stiff in my neck and my lower back, but I didn't think much of it at first. It got worse over the next day or two.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or therapist since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to my primary care doctor and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week. The doctor diagnosed a neck and back strain.

Q: Do you have any prior injuries or problems with your neck or back?
A: I had some stiffness years ago after a minor fall, but it had resolved and I hadn't been treated for it recently.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I've had trouble sleeping and some days I can't work the way I normally do. I just want my treatment covered.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
